elements.element: Customer is not subject to any restriction on soliciting Vendor employees or personnel.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 expressly provides that Customer “shall not solicit” covered Vendor personnel.

elements.element: Customer is prohibited from soliciting covered Vendor personnel.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 prohibits Customer solicitation, subject to the subsequently stated scope limitations and exceptions.

elements.element: Vendor is prohibited from soliciting covered Customer personnel.
elements.evidence: The clause makes the restriction mutual and states that “neither party shall solicit personnel of the other party.”

elements.element: The restriction applies only to personnel of the other party who are directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Section 12.4 “is limited to personnel directly involved in the Services.”

elements.element: The restriction runs for 12 months from the end of each covered individual's involvement in the Services.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the restriction “runs for 12 months from the end of that individual's involvement in the Services rather than from the end of the term.” This expressly qualifies the earlier term-based wording.

elements.element: General advertisements and other general recruitment activities not targeted at the other party's personnel are carved out.
elements.evidence: The clause permits hiring a person who responds to “a general advertisement or other general recruitment activity not targeted at the other party's personnel.”

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches by personnel are carved out.
elements.evidence: The clause permits hiring a person “who makes an unsolicited approach to a party.”

elements.element: Neither party is subject to a no-hire obligation.
elements.evidence: The operative text deletes the original prohibition on hiring or employing and expressly states that “neither party is subject to any no-hire obligation.”

result.reason: The preferred position is not met because Customer remains bound by a non-solicit. Every fallback requirement is present in the operative language. The changes are confined to converting the original unilateral, broad, 24-month no-solicit/no-hire into the specified mutual and limited non-solicit. Drafting quality is reduced because the opening sentence retains inconsistent scope and timing language (“any Vendor employee,” during the term and 12 months afterward) that is only corrected by the following sentence; the express limitation and “rather than” wording make the provisions reconcilable, but direct replacement would be clearer.
